claims.text: THE QUALIFICATION, WHICH TRAVELS WITH THE ARTICLE AND IS ROUTINELY DROPPED. The description is what Lazar told the reporter, not an employment record. Stanton Friedman, who obtained the Los Alamos telephone directory page carrying Lazar's name, records that the page 'clearly states that it includes employees of the DOE and outside contractor, Kirk Meyer'. A Los Alamos colleague interviewed on tape by Mark Farmer on 25 May 1996 said Lazar 'was a contractor' under 'Kirk Mayer' and that he 'claimed to be' a physicist. Tom Mahood's 2018 conclusion is that Lazar worked as an electronic technician for Kirk-Mayer and that the Monitor article misrepresented his position on the basis of what he told the reporter.

claims.sourceText: Stanton T. claims.text: Bob Lazar's connection to the laboratory must be stated as 'named in a directory', never as 'employed by'. He appears in a 1982 Los Alamos telephone directory whose own text states that it covers Department of Energy employees and the outside contractor Kirk-Mayer; a colleague interviewed on tape in 1996 said Lazar 'was a contractor' under Kirk Mayer; and the laboratory later said it held no records for him. The Los Alamos Monitor of 27 June 1982 described him in the newspaper's own voice as 'a physicist at the Los Alamos Meson Physics Facility', which is what he told the reporter.

claims.text: A Los Alamos colleague of Lazar's, interviewed on tape by Mark Farmer on 25 May 1996 and anonymised at his own request, said Lazar did work at the laboratory but 'was a contractor' under 'Kirk Mayer', and that Lazar 'claimed to be' a physicist with a degree from 'either Cal Tech or MIT or something like that, but I don't think that that was ever substantiated that he had a degree'.
